sentences.text: Triodus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Xenacanthiformes, a group of elasmobranchs.
This genus is part of the extinct family Xenacanthidae, which served as its parent group.
Unlike many modern sharks, these animals lived exclusively in freshwater environments.
The genus Triodus was first described by Jordan in 1849.
Fossils of Triodus have been found in the Chinle Formation and Black Prince Limestone of Arizona, the Petrified Forest Member of New Mexico, and the Tecovas Formation of Texas in the United States.
The time range for Triodus extends from the Bashkirian to the Norian stages, between 323.4 and 205.7 million years ago.
A new species named Triodus richterae was described in 2017 from fossils found in the Rio do Rasto Formation in Brazil.
